{{Quote|At times, Mother Talzin shows more concern for reputation than for the will of the Spirits.|Asajj Ventress|<ref name="BOS" />}}
The '''Spirits''' were supernatural beings which the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] thought to exist. It was a common opinion amongst both [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] that the "Spirits" were based on an archaic and [[Shaman of the Nightsisters|shamanistic]] interpretation of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. The witches believed the Spirits bestowed their blessings on Dathomir and allowed the practice of [[Dathomir Magic|magicks]] by tapping into their energy.

==Overview==
{{Quote|It is a core truth of the Nightsisters that the spirit plane exists parallel to our own.|Mother Talzin|<ref name="BOS" />}}
[[File:Fanged_God_Book_of_Sith.jpg|thumb|left|160px|The Fanged God, a spirit of masculine energy and chaos]]
According to the beliefs of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], there was another realm, a parallel plane to the physical world that was inhabited by spirits. This spiritual realm was thought to be governed in balance by the [[The Ones/Legends|Twin Deities]], the [[Daughter/Legends|Winged Goddess]] and the [[Son/Legends|Fanged God]], which were depictions of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|Light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="BOS" />

In her instructional treatise entitled ''[[Wild Power]]'', [[Mother (title)/Legends|Clan Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] implied there was a single representative spirit for each animal [[Species/Legends|species]] in the spirit realm, something she calls the "ur-spirit." These ur-spirits were the other inhabitants of the spiritual realm, under the rule of the Twin Deities. The ur-spirits of animals, according to Talzin, are "red and raw," while that of plants "pulses with a deep green" and is "quieter and more content." All spirits and their physical counterparts constituted Dathomir's "life web."<ref name="BOS" />

The Nightsisters also believed the two realms were so close on [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] that only their [[Shaman of the Nightsisters|shamans]] could carry messages between them. The shamans of the Nightsisters were thought to have been "chosen" to encounter and interact with the spirit world. They were thought to act as a conduit for the Spirits themselves.<ref name="BOS" />

==Powers==
{{Quote|The spirits bestow fertility upon our tribe and visit us when sickness and death come upon one of our sisters as well as to claim the spirits of those who have fallen.|Mother Talzin|<ref name="BOS" />}}
According to the lore, the Spirits bestowed fertility upon the clans and claimed the souls of the [[Death/Legends|dead]]. Nightsisters talismans were thought to have been empowered by the spirits. [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] thought those artifacts were not very different from the ones made by the ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], but no [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemist]] had ever been known to duplicate the non-conventional effects of the Nightsisters' talismans, such as [[metamorphosis]]. Such a supernatural, alchemic-power deficiency among the Sith throughout their history Sidious thought "curious".<ref name="BOS" />

==Existence==
{{Quote|My master Ky Narec did not believe in the spirits, nor did Count Dooku or the people of Rattatak. In my eagerness to become something other than what I am, I fear I have forgotten the truth of my childhood.|Asajj Ventress|<ref name="BOS" />}}
[[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], born a Nightsister and trained successively as as [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi apprentice]] and a [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolyte]],<ref name="Nightsisters">{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}}</ref> once wrote that her former masters [[Ky Narec/Legends|Ky Narec]] and [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] did not believe in the Spirits. Indeed, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] thought the work of the Spirits was a primitive name for the [[Unifying Force/Legends|Unifying Force]] and the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]].<ref name="BOS" /> The Twin Deities, however, were confirmed to exist during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], when [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was [[Mission to Mortis/Legends|brought]] to [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]], a mysterious planet enclosed in a [[Mortis monolith/Legends|octahedral monolith]].<ref name="Overlords">{{TCW|Overlords}}</ref>

There were many parallels between the Spirits and the Force. [[Clan mother/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] would say a Nightsister had to serve the will of the Spirits, just like a Jedi would serve the will of the Force. Moreover, it was said that [[Allya/Legends|Allya]] foretold the rise of a perfect being "brought into existence by the Spirits", which was very reminiscent of the prophecy of the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]].<ref name="BOS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Talzin believes in a spirit realm inhabited by the life-energies of animals and ruled by the universal manifestations of male and female energy.|[[Daniel Wallace]]|<ref name="Geek">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 4)|date=2010-04-23}}</ref>}}
The Spirits worshipped by the Nightsisters were described in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''. As the part of the book in which they appear is written from a Nightsister's perspective, it is unclear if the spirits do exist or if they are just archaic manifestations of the Force. The book also directly links the spirits with the "Mortis Trilogy", a story-arc of the TV series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''.
